newsitem.title: UK: Hunters vs. saboteurs in Britain's 'Glorious 12th'.
newsitem.headline: Hunters vs. saboteurs in Britain's 'Glorious 12th'.

text.p: Marksmen across Britain took aim on Tuesday to launch the "Glorious Twelfth", opening day of the grouse-shooting season and a social must for the rich sportsman.
But "bagging" a pair of birds may be harder this year as hunt saboteurs have spread out across the northern English moors to disrupt shoots.

"We've got 80-100 saboteurs in a valley in North Yorkshire with large numbers of police and stewards. There is a game of cat and mouse going on. The shooters are hiding from us right now," said a Hunt Saboteurs' spokesman speaking from a mobile phone.
He explained that the group stands in front of the shooters' guns to prevent them from firing.
Participants in the aristocratic sport also face a reduced grouse population, hard hit by cold, wet weather.
By the time the shooting-season ends on December 10 an estimated 450,000 grouse will have been shot.

Conservationists, who dub the day "Inglorious Twelfth", claim gamekeepers target animals that prey on the grouse and that burning of the moors to ensure enough heather for the grouse destroys the vital habitat of other birds.
But gamekeepers say Britain's 459 grouse moors conserve habitats for a variety of birds including larks, plovers and pipits. ($ = 0.632 British Pounds)
